clue.text: It was good to settle for a meal in middle of day

definitions.text: It was good to settle for a meal in middle of day

parts.words: It was good to settle for a meal in middle of day
parts.note: a paper token, once handed to British workers, that could be exchanged for food at midday; 'good to settle' plays on a bill being paid

explanation.definitionFit: Describes the old British employee perk of a voucher redeemable for a midday meal in cafés.

clue.text: Officer arrests us, almost drunk and lecherous

indicators.note: an officer who arrests someone holds them, so the officer's letters go round the next word

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the following synonym is dropped

parts.note: drunk means full, i.e. tanked up

explanation.surface: A police officer, nearly drunk himself, collars a pair of lecherous suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous and the answer are synonyms, both meaning full of sexual desire.

clue.text: Railwaymen have points to look after

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
S, south, is a compass point
E, east, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Railway workers are given directions to care for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a patient or care for someone is a synonym of look after.

clue.text: Where American girls tend to anticipate marriage

definitions.text: Where American girls tend to anticipate marriage

parts.words: Where American girls tend to anticipate marriage
parts.note: a US chest in which a young woman collects linen and household goods ahead of a wedding, the British bottom drawer; 'anticipate' hints at hoping

explanation.definitionFit: Describes the American storage chest where a young woman gathers her trousseau before marrying.

clue.text: A giant, so it appears, when standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean so

explanation.surface: A big figure, so it seems, when he gets to his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when standing up' turns ERGO, giving the letters of the answer; 'it appears' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairytale giant that eats people is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: Archdeacon initially impatient with colleague, excusably

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven.

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of impatient

parts.note: an ally is a colleague or partner

explanation.surface: An archdeacon, impatient from the start, joins a fellow cleric, and can be forgiven for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a pardonable one, so the adverb means in a forgivable way.

clue.text: Shock to university crowd

parts.note: to be up is to be at university, in British usage
a set is a group or crowd of people

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd of students causes a shock at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to upset or disturb them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Passes on effortlessly

definitions.meaning: a verb phrase: gives to the next generation

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: bequeaths to descendants, and with ease as in a jockey's untroubled win.

clue.text: Tirade about a girl beaming with joy

indicators.note: about means the tirade goes round the following letters

parts.note: a rant is a tirade
taken as written
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl, surprisingly, is all smiles after a rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant describes a face glowing or beaming with happiness.

clue.text: Discard niblick for recycling

parts.note: to scrap something is to discard it
a niblick is an old name for a golf iron

explanation.surface: A golfer throws an old club onto the recycling heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste metal sent for remelting is exactly what the whole clue describes: a junked iron club.

clue.text: It sounds wrong to answer back to ecclesiastical council

indicators.note: it sounds signals that the next word is heard spoken rather than spelled

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: back signals that the next word is read in reverse

parts.note: to do is to answer, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: A church council may find it wrong to answer back.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy convened to decide church matters.

clue.text: Warm coat to take to the cleaners

definitions.meaning: a warm jacket of synthetic pile, or a sheep's wool
to swindle someone out of their money

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a cosy jacket or sheep's coat; the verb means to cheat or overcharge.

clue.text: Fanciful composition as a faint diversion

indicators.note: a diversion sends things off course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whimsical piece of music provides a light diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasia is a free-form musical piece of imaginative, improvised character.

clue.text: Artillery equipment easily bent

definitions.meaning: a two-wheeled cart that a gun is hitched to

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the detachable front part of a gun carriage; the adjective means lithe.

clue.text: Men of the cloth may not mind being so repellent

definitions.text: Men of the cloth may not mind being so repellent

parts.words: Men of the cloth may not mind being so repellent
parts.note: men of the cloth seem to be clergy, but here are insects that eat fabric, and the repellent is a treatment against them

explanation.definitionFit: Describes fabric treated to repel clothes moths, which feed on cloth.

clue.text: Jet not working — power failure

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
out means not functioning or on strike

explanation.surface: A jet aircraft stops working when the power fails.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss of electricity supply plunging an area into darkness is a common synonym.

clue.text: Agreement with Rome doctor can ringing wreck

indicators.note: to wreck something is to ruin it, so the letters are broken and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's ringing a can could wreck a deal with the Vatican.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a treaty between the Pope and a state, an agreement with Rome.

clue.text: Judge at dance frolicking cheek by jowl

indicators.note: frolicking suggests romping about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge at a dance gets close to his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek by jowl means very close together, side by side, next to each other.

clue.text: Haigha's showed typical Anglo-Saxon truculence

parts.note: Haigha is the Anglo-Saxon Messenger in Through the Looking-Glass whose odd postures Alice calls Anglo-Saxon; truculence suggests bolshie behaviour

explanation.definitionFit: Points to a posture or a defiant manner, the two senses linking Lewis Carroll's messenger and truculence.

clue.text: One responding to pressure from tyrant to help out

indicators.note: help out puts the helping word outside the tyrant

parts.note: aid means help
Nero was the tyrannical Roman emperor

explanation.surface: Someone yields to pressure from a tyrant to provide assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneroid barometer measures air pressure by a sealed capsule that flexes in response.

clue.text: Remove tie in a French sort of garden

parts.note: un is French for a
a knot garden is a formal garden of intricately laid hedges

explanation.surface: A man loosens his tie in a formal French garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie a knot or a bond is a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: House where you may get knifed

definitions.meaning: a playhouse where dramas are staged
the operating room where a surgeon cuts

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a playhouse, and also a hospital room where surgery is done.

clue.text: Many peer amazedly in the heavens

indicators.note: amazedly suggests confusion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of people stare up in wonder at the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the highest heaven, so as an adjective it means celestial.

clue.text: Engineers' ladder put out again

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: Army engineers carry a ladder outside again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun a programme is to broadcast it once more.

clue.text: Funny English fruit

parts.note: comic means funny

explanation.surface: An amusing English fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comice is a variety of pear, an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Alice turned out to be gutsy

indicators.note: turned out suggests something changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Alice proved to be a brave girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac means relating to the ileum, part of the intestine, hence humorously gutsy.

clue.text: Party of us outside find a bouquet

indicators.note: outside puts the 'of us' word round the party

parts.note: our means belonging to us
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Partygoers get outside to find a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouquet is a wine's smell, so a synonym of scent or smell.

clue.text: Handy means, short of time, to hurry along books

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to expedite is to speed up or hurry along
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A convenient way to rush some books through without much time.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedient is a convenient, practical means to an end.
